newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh leader aims to halve annual inflation.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh leader aims to halve annual inflation.

text.p: Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev said his government aimed to halve inflation annually so annual inflation will be between four to six percent by 2000.
"The annual level of inflation must fall by no less than half," Nazarbayev said in a "statement to the people" published in the official daily Kazakhstanskaya Pravda on Tuesday.
Annual inflation of 2,200 percent for 1993 dropped to 60 percent in 1995. Both the government and western financial institutions predicted 1996 annual inflation near 30 percent.
Nazarbayev said the government aimed to slash annual inflation to four to six percent by 2000 and establish growth of three to five percent in the same period.

The Kazakh president said by the first half of 1998 at the latest, privatisation and reform of the country's industrial and financial sectors should be completed, with the "harshest measures" used to close down bankrupt enterprises.

The president's statement came the same day as the Central Asian nation's most powerful trade unions announced a series of demonstrations across the former Soviet republic on Oct 17 to protest the non-payment of salaries and pensions.
"The non-payments crisis has taken on a chronic and systemic character which affects not only a large number of enterprises but all sectors," Nazarbayev said in his statement.
